direction.comments: The direction on a macroscale is amazing, building such a detailed, handcrafted world that's phenomenal, though it's a double-edged sword, as a majority of the movie is chase sequences and grand shots meant to make you feel in awe of how vast, expansive, and detailed this world is, which makes it feel like they're just showing off the animation (an issue I also had with The Wild Robot); the direction on a microscale is not great, as it feels so pretentious, edgy, and self-consciously quirky, constantly trying to subvert traditional dialogue with characters interjecting to show they're different and weird, and between the dialogue and the voice acting, there's no real chemistry in the cast and you don't care about the characters; the storytelling is fine, as the movie being one giant chase sequence immerses you in the world, which is cool to an extent, but it gets repetitive once you get the world, and the actual story itself feels a little forced, with a lot of telling you what the story is; the tension is actually pretty good, as even though the character writing isn't good, the emotional buildup in the tense scenes works, especially in the last 20 to 30 minutes

performance.comments: Fine, but her performance is very standard and doesn't elevate the movie much, as I didn't feel she brought a lot to the table or made me care about the character at all

Plays the nerdy kid how it's written, but I just didn't believe it, as the voice acting felt very forced, templated, and generic without adding much to the story, and he has no chemistry with Peyton Elizabeth Lee, feeling like they each recorded their lines separately and stitched them together
Fine, but gives a very standard performance
I do not understand how she keeps getting these voice-acting roles, as she plays the same Awkwafina character she always does
Also gives a very standard performance

cast.comments: The voice acting as a whole was a big drawback, as it wasn't mixed in well and wasn't great quality, with nobody truly taking the movie over the edge, and combined with the poorly written characters, it made me not care about these characters or the narrative; it's an expensive cast, and while I get that big names draw in more eyes, they should have just hired voice actors who could have done a way better job for a lot cheaper

story.comments: The concept is a double-edged sword of wanting original movies, as I enjoyed that it's an original concept, but it overcomplicates things by shoving a lot into this world and explaining it very fast, while borrowing so much from the fantasy genre that it ends up pretty standard and doesn't bring anything really new; the plot structure is mostly linear, with some flashbacks to give you context; character writing is not good, as it's full of templated, stereotypical characters, from the main girl who is exactly what you expect when the movie starts to the basic nerdy friend, and they shove so many characters into Wildwood that you don't really care about anyone, which is an issue since caring about the characters is so important to caring about the story

screenplay.comments: The dialogue is not good, as it feels like video game dialogue trying to be cool, hip, and weird, overcomplicating things to sound smarter and more original than it needs to, and while the movie is very dark and mature, the clunky dialogue feels like it was written for teens with the occasional swear word or more adult wording; the humor is fine, as the hit rate isn't amazing, but it works; the symbolism is very strong for such a surprisingly dark and mature movie, touching on loss, greed, acceptance, the five stages of grief, letting go, and maturity, with death as a big topic and a lot of death and killing shown on screen, to the point where I was surprised it was rated PG-13; the foreshadowing is pretty good, as they plant a lot of roots from the beginning that grow into a tree that lays the foundation for the ending

score.comments: Actually good, as I very much enjoyed how well composed it was and how well it built the world

soundtrack.comments: The songs feel a little forced at moments, like they were added to make a play for Best Original Song at the Oscars, but they were fine, not adding too much or taking away too much

cinematography.comments: Very good, especially in how it's shot with stop-motion, playing a big hand in creating the world and the animation, to the point where it feels like a real-life movie carefully captured through stop-motion

editing.comments: Works in conjunction with the cinematography to make the movie feel very fluid and seamless for a stop-motion movie, especially with how grand and massive some of the sequences are, though the flashback sequences were kind of tacky (a very minor point)

sound.comments: The ADR and sound mixing for the voice acting are not good, as it's very obvious the dialogue was dubbed over and not mixed properly; outside of that, the sound design is what you'd expect from a stop-motion movie

animation.comments: Phenomenal, a true triumph and magnum opus in stop-motion animation that needs to be studied and applauded, as how detailed and expansive the world is and the scenes they're able to create are truly breathtaking; this isn't a knock on the animation, but the movie relies on a lot of chase sequences and battles to show it off, which hurts the storytelling, and while that trade-off makes sense for a movie showing off its animation capabilities, it still hurts the movie overall

review.pacing: Paced decently well without dragging much, but it shoves a lot of plot at you and overcomplicates things, making it feel slower than it needs to be, so cutting 10 to 15 minutes and keeping it simpler would have helped
review.climax: Phenomenal, with genuinely some of the best animation I've ever seen, as the grand battle sequence being entirely stop-motion animated is truly breathtaking and makes sticking with the movie feel worth it
review.tone: Very dark, as I was shocked by how many adult, mature themes it deals with, since you usually equate animation with family movies, but this is not a family movie; it's very much for young adults and adults, stretching its PG-13 rating to the point where it feels R-rated at moments with how bloody some scenes get
review.final_notes: Saw at Regal with a ticket from Pixel Scene Media for the work I've done promoting Wildwood
review.overall: Overall, 'Wildwood' is a triumph and genuinely a magnum opus in stop-motion animation that needs to be celebrated for how breathtaking and beautiful it is; however, it's very much a style-over-substance movie, as it shows off its animation so much that the endless chase sequences take away from the storytelling, while the poorly written dialogue and stiff voice acting keep you from caring about any of the characters
